title: Does Liking Yellow Imply Driving a School Bus? Semantic Leakage in Language Models

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.1 (temperatures 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5; 10 runs per prompt); max_tokens assumed (generations are truncated after the first period)

task.subset_rule: all: 109 test prompts with their 30 matched control prompts; 10 samples at each of 4 temperatures for every prompt
task.approximation: max_tokens is not stated; the BERTScore backbone follows the evaluate-metric default (roberta-large); test and control samples are paired by sample index within a temperature.

items.source: https://gonenhila.github.io/files/semantic_leakage_prompts.txt (footnote 2; 139 lines: 109 test prompts + 30 control prompts, each prefixed 'Complete the sentence:')

fields_prose.input: prompt line (test) and its control line
fields_prose.label: concept (the inserted clause, e.g. 'koalas'; derived by diffing test and control)

items.filter_prose: control prompt = the first line of each block (the variant without the concept clause); every following line of the block is a test prompt matched to it; in the idiom section each literal/idiom pair is (control, test)
items.structure_verified: plain text, 140 lines (109 test + 30 control prompts + blank separators), e.g. 'Complete the sentence: His favorite food is' (control) followed by 'Complete the sentence: He likes koalas. His favorite food is' (tests)

placeholders.prompt_line: items.line (NOT expressible: .txt is not a supported table format)

prompt.source_location: Section 3 / footnote 2 (prompt file) and Table 1 examples
prompt.verbatim: full (prompt file served by the author's site; the paper's examples omit the 'Complete the sentence:' prefix that the file carries)

placeholders_prose.prompt_line: the full line from the file, e.g. 'Complete the sentence: He likes koalas. His favorite food is' (test) or 'Complete the sentence: His favorite food is' (control)

output.parse_prose: free text: remove a repeated prompt, truncate after the first period (Sec. 3.1)

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Leak-Rate (BERTScore): for each test prompt, temperature and sample index i, score 1 if BERTScore-F1(concept, test generation_i) > BERTScore-F1(concept, control generation_i), 0 if smaller, 0.5 if equal; average over the 109 x 4 x 10 instances, x100 (Eq. 1; Table 2 caption).

open_points: Parameter sweep: four temperatures x 10 samples per prompt cannot be expressed (model.params is one parameter set; a hook cannot change the request body), and the Leak-Rate needs BERTScore-F1 with roberta-large (torch/transformers), outside the stdlib/numpy/pandas hook rules. The plain-text prompt file itself would be a trivial load_items (139 lines: 30 control + 109 test prompts, concept = the clause that differs).
notes: Per seed: (109 + 30) prompts x 4 temperatures x 10 samples = 5,560 short calls (est_calls counts 3 seeds; the temperature-0 replicates are near-duplicates). bootstrap item = test prompt (40 instances each).
